sections.title: Basic Concept of Probability
sections.content: Probability means the chance of an event occurring. The basic formula is: Probability = Favorable Outcomes / Total Outcomes. The value always lies between 0 and 1. If an event is certain, Probability = 1, and if it is impossible, Probability = 0.

sections.title: Sample Space and Favorable Outcomes
sections.content: Sample Space (S) is the set of all possible outcomes. Favorable Outcomes are the results that satisfy the condition of the question. First write the total outcomes, then count the favorable outcomes, and then apply the formula.

sections.title: Coin Toss (1, 2, 3 Coins)
sections.content:
1 coin: Sample Space = {H, T}, total outcomes = 2.
2 coins: {HH, HT, TH, TT}, total = 4.
3 coins: total outcomes = 8 (2^3).
Example: Probability of getting 1 Head in 2 coins = 2/4 = 1/2.

sections.title: Dice Roll (1 or 2 Dice)
sections.content:
1 die: Sample Space = {1,2,3,4,5,6}, total = 6.
Probability of a prime number (2,3,5) = 3/6 = 1/2.
2 dice: total outcomes = 36 (6×6). Favorable outcomes for sum 7 = 6, so Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

sections.title: Deck of 52 Cards
sections.content:
Total cards = 52. There are 4 suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades). Each suit has 13 cards.
Face Cards = J, Q, K (total 12).
Example: Probability of a Red card = 26/52 = 1/2.

sections.title: Mutually Exclusive and Exhaustive Events
sections.content:
Mutually Exclusive: Two events cannot occur together. Formula: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
Exhaustive Events: All possible outcomes are included. Example: Head or Tail.

sections.title: Complementary Event
sections.content:
If A is an event, then the Probability of Not A = 1 − P(A).
Example: Probability of not getting 6 on a die = 1 − (1/6) = 5/6.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Counting the Sample Space incorrectly.
2. Counting favorable outcomes more than once.
3. Not using complement when it makes the problem easier.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Always write the Sample Space first. Then count favorable outcomes. Then apply Probability = Favorable / Total. Use complement and addition rules correctly.

tricks.title: At Least 1 Head in 2 Coins
tricks.explanation: Instead of counting directly, use complement.

tricks.title: Mutually Exclusive Addition Rule
tricks.explanation: If A and B cannot occur together, add their probabilities.

tricks.title: Use Complement Quickly
tricks.explanation: When counting favorable outcomes is difficult.
